stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for enhanced performance.
This update specifically targets and optimizes execution on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device for privacy.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major social media platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are accused of obstructing researchers.
The core issue is the alleged failure of these tech giants to provide legally mandated data.
This highlights ongoing regulatory and transparency challenges facing Big Tech in Europe.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework designed to enhance 3D spatial awareness in VLMs.
Achieves this enhancement by integrating both implicit and explicit 3D geometries, utilizing Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs).

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based inputs which struggle with scene complexity and occlusion.
The method introduces a graph-based approach for flexible and precise control over multiple subjects in video generation.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of simply reducing sycophancy in LLMs, proposing a need for more nuanced moral reasoning.
The study investigates the 'resistance-compliance' process, focusing on how models decide when to accept external perspectives versus maintaining their own judgment.
Model judgment revision is shown to be structured across three dimensions, suggesting a deeper, multi-faceted approach to social calibration in AI.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, proprietary inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) using open infrastructure.
Enables training in diverse environments by natively supporting the stateful, multi-process nature of harness-based agent inference.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D-based Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries into VLMs.
Employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to inject high-level geometric priors into the model for enhanced 3D awareness.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models specifically designed for African languages.
The models utilize the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder and cover 27 language varieties across several African nations.
Training data primarily consists of read speech from religious texts, ensuring broad coverage and license clearance.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical scaling issue in speculative decoding when dealing with very long contexts (millions of tokens).
The problem arises because standard Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads incur a linear cost due to full attention over the entire KV cache.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' aims to mitigate this 'Draft-KV Tax' to maintain efficiency at massive context lengths.

stories.title: Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB, Affecting Shizuku, libadb and Developers
stories.author: kitsumed.github.io via raymii
bullet_points: Android is reportedly considering restrictions on On-Device ADB access.
This change could significantly impact third-party tools like Shizuku and libadb.
The development signals a potential shift in how developers interact with Android internals.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon devices.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: After backlash, Meta pauses plan to ‘rate limit’ its smart glasses
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has paused its plan to implement a $20 monthly subscription fee for its smart glasses feature.
The feature in question allows users to hear each other more clearly and operates locally on the glasses.
The pause comes following public backlash against the proposed monetization strategy.

stories.title: Meta just created a moderation nightmare for its smart glasses
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: Meta's smart glasses are facing significant public backlash regarding privacy concerns.
The devices are being misused by bad actors to film and prank unsuspecting strangers.
There are specific concerns about women being targeted as content for these unauthorized recordings.

stories.title: With help from data, art museums are reframing the visitor experience
stories.author: Mureji Fatunde-Iloeje
bullet_points: Art museums are integrating data analytics into their operations.
The trend involves data-driven curation of exhibits and visitor experiences.
This reflects a broader shift in how cultural institutions are adopting technology.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update emphasizes token efficiency improvements rather than a massive jump in raw capability.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective models are often sufficient for many practical applications.
This signals a market trend where efficiency and cost-effectiveness are becoming as important as peak performance in LLMs.

stories.title: Roku raises streaming stick prices by up to 60 percent
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Roku is significantly increasing the price of its streaming sticks by up to 60%.
The company attributes the price hike to a shortage of RAM.
The announcement contrasts with a previous positive outlook from the CEO regarding the business.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent performance in visual reasoning, even when equivalent information is presented in text, diagram, or combined formats.
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different input views (text vs. visual) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning capabilities in VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, indicating that current models do not integrate reasoning robustly across different data modalities.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across distributions of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
This work aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by incorporating 'necessity' alongside 'sufficiency' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a new foundation model for molecular property prediction that handles conformational ensembles.
The model uses Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNN) to encode individual conformers before pooling them with a Set Attention Block.
It is pretrained on CREMP, a dataset specifically focused on cyclic peptide ensembles, addressing limitations of single-conformation modeling.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study, titled MIRROR, suggests that different views (text, diagram, combined) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning pathways in VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, where strong performance in one modality does not guarantee success in another.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the current limitation of audio-language models in deep logical reasoning compared to text-based LLMs.
Introduces X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework.
The framework transfers reasoning capabilities from a strong text teacher model to a weaker audio-language student model.

stories.title: The Boundaries of Automation: A Theory of Persistent Human Participation
stories.author: Iryna Gurevych
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing assumption that human involvement in AI is solely due to current system limitations.
It shifts the focus from 'how far automation can extend' to defining the conceptual limits of automation.
The research posits that human participation may remain necessary even when AI systems achieve high levels of capability.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM applications in medicine, moving beyond simple Q&A to structured, longitudinal learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to synthesize case-grounded clinical stories.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to facilitate end-to-end training of AI agents.
It specifically addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables agents to be trained in diverse environments while natively supporting the multi-process nature of harness-based reasoning and tool use.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research introduces GS-Agent, a method to generate dynamic and physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language prompts.
Existing generative methods struggle with ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in simulated environments.
The work addresses the limitations of traditional computer graphics, which require extensive manual human effort.

stories.title: Artificial Epanorthosis: Why large language models overuse a classical rhetorical figure, and how to mitigate it
stories.author: Federico Boggia
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit a systematic overuse of the classical rhetorical figure, epanorthosis (self-correction).
The overuse is attributed to training data rich in promotional prose and RLHF tuning that favors emphatic language.
The study suggests the left-to-right generation process contributes to this rhetorical pattern.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates whether different independently trained code language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent the same concepts consistently across different programming languages (Python and Rust).
The study uses a 2x2 design and extends concept-circuit extraction to systematically analyze how task, language, and model influence code model representations.
The findings aim to disentangle the specific roles of the task, the language syntax, and the underlying model architecture in how code is encoded.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy constraint of using cloud-based LLMs for coding tasks involving sensitive or personal data.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as a viable alternative for data preparation tasks.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the performance of AI agents running on these local models.

stories.title: Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB
stories.author: shscs911
bullet_points: Android is reportedly planning to introduce restrictions on On-Device ADB.
This change suggests a move towards tighter security and control over device access.
The development is a significant topic within the Android developer and security communities.

stories.title: I built a production AI agent as a Honda service advisor. Then I read the textbook.
stories.author: andersonasprilla
bullet_points: The article details the practical experience of deploying a production AI agent in a customer-facing role (Honda service advisor).
A key learning derived from the build is the necessity of robust code guarantees complementing LLM classification capabilities.
The author highlights the gap between practical implementation and formal AI engineering knowledge, noting missing theoretical components.
